message.content:
I need a detailed, concrete implementation plan for a two-phase project on Nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres hosting platform, production at /opt/nxeon, staging at /opt/nxeon-staging with NXEON_SANDBOX=1). This is plan-mode research/design only — do not write any code, do not modify any files.

## Background (already researched by prior exploration agents — treat as established fact, don't re-derive)

**Current portal state:**
- `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` has a `NavSection[]` array (lines 33-96): 7 groups — Dashboard, Compute (Deploy/Servers/Shared Hosting/Game Servers/Server Directory/Volumes), Build, Network, Mail, Tools, Account. Icons are hand-drawn inline SVGs keyed by string name via an `Icon()` helper in `components/portal/Shell.tsx:182` — there is NO icon library (no lucide-react/heroicons) anywhere in the codebase.
- Design tokens live in `app/globals.css` (Tailwind v4, no config file, `@theme`/CSS custom properties): `--color-brand-50…900` (violet, #6f47f5 at 500), `--color-navy-950…600`, `--color-accent-blue` (#3b82f6), `--color-accent-cyan` (#22d3ee). Shared classes: `.card`, `.glass`, `.btn-primary/.btn-secondary/.btn-danger/.btn-ghost/.btn-deploy`, `.input`, `.nav-item`, `.section-label`, `.page-title`. Shared components: `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (PageHeader, StatCard, StatusDot, Badge, EmptyState) and `components/ui/charts.tsx` (hand-rolled SVG charts, CLAUDE.md explicitly says don't add a chart library). `components/portal/PortalHero.tsx` is a per-page header banner used consistently across pages (variant prop swaps illustration/accent/eyebrow).
- `app/dashboard/page.tsx` (298 lines, overview) and `app/dashboard/servers/page.tsx` (thin, delegates to `ServersList`) are clean examples. `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx` (944 lines) is the worst "organically bolted-on" page — one long vertical scroll of `.card` sections (payment method, auto-recharge, spend controls, transactions, renewals, coupons, invoices) with no tabs. `app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx` already uses a `?tab=` server-rendered tab pattern (Profile/Security/Integrations/Notifications) — a better pattern worth replicating.

**Purchase/deploy wizards** (`components/customer/`): `DeployWizard.tsx` (VPS), `HostingDeployWizard.tsx`, `GameDeployWizard.tsx`, `DomainRegisterWizard.tsx` each have their OWN copy-pasted local `Stepper` function — 4 near-identical forks. `DomainTransferInWizard.tsx` and `MigrationWizard.tsx` hand-roll their own different numbered-circle step markup. `PaymentStep.tsx` is the one genuinely shared/reused component (embedded card/PayPal/Coinbase UI) across VPS/Hosting/Game/Domain-Register wizards. All four are mounted from a single hub: `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` → `components/customer/DeployHub.tsx` (368 lines) — a hero + 4-card product-type tab selector (VPS/Hosting/Game/Email), deep-linked via `?product=`, already a reasonably good entry point.

**Trust/conversion components** (`components/customer/`): `WizardTrustBar.tsx` (superseded, no longer rendered — kept for its documented honesty rules), `WizardReassuranceCard.tsx` (current active version — icon+claim strip: Uptime/Support/Setup), `PaymentTrustBar.tsx` (payment-step-only: "Secured by Stripe", card logos), `WizardStickyCart.tsx` (sticky price+Continue bar). CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: these components have hard-won, explicitly-documented honesty rules — a money-back-guarantee claim was investigated and deliberately removed multiple times (three prior removal sites cited in comments) because no such policy is actually published/honored anywhere. There are currently ZERO fabricated social-proof elements anywhere (no testimonials, no countdown timers, no fake scarcity/"X people bought this") — the only real social proof is genuine "Popular"/featured badges on plan tiers.

**Sandbox/isolation infrastructure:** `lib/sandbox.ts` (`SANDBOX = process.env.NXEON_SANDBOX === "1"`) gates ~20 branches in `worker/index.ts` (provision/remove/resize/snapshot/backup/etc. — all genuinely inert: no real Proxmox, OVH, Cloudflare DNS, SSH, cPanel calls) plus several other lib/worker files (cloudflare-oauth, cpanel-inline, hosting-db, backup-schedule, databases, game-subdomain-sync, game-mods, restore, websites). CRITICAL GAP: Stripe itself is NOT code-gated anywhere — `lib/actions.ts`'s `payAndDeploy` (~L516-612) only skips Stripe when the wallet fully covers the price (`cardCents <= 0`, computed via `walletSplit`), calling `stripe().checkout.sessions.create` otherwise; there is no SANDBOX check around Stripe at all. Existing fake-balance mechanisms: `lib/actions-sandbox.ts`'s `sandboxTopUp(cents)` (self-serve $1-1000 repeatable, SANDBOX-only) and `lib/actions.ts`'s `adminCreditUser`/`adminGrantFreeVps` (admin-only, work in any env). Existing subdomain pattern to copy: a hand-written nginx vhost `nxeon-staging-admin` proxies `staging.4j3d7gkr2wcbi34.nxeon.cloud` to the SAME backend as `staging.nxeon.cloud` under a different hostname/cert, purely to avoid admin/customer session collision — this is the template for adding a new hostname, since `scripts/configure-domains.sh`/`domains.env` only supports 3 fixed hostnames (BASE/ADMIN/STAGING) and doesn't generalize to a 4th automatically.

## The user's actual request (their exact words, read carefully)

"I want you to do a complete overhaul on the UI/UX of some pages in the customer portal. I want these to be mockups until i agree to them, so see if you can display them privately somewhere. You need to take the entire scope of the system into consideration to plan and map things out. The problem with the ui/ux right now is that it wasnt planned. we continuously built on top of it, so anytime we added a new feature or page, it was just thrown somewhere without much thought for the flow of everything. I want you to make flows better, easier to understand, i also want this to be a complete redesign as well, creating new icons from scatch, scraping together beautiful images that are relevant to the context of the feature/page. take into consideration buyer psychology to maximize conversions. Look at what we have so far for all of the entire customer portal right now, keep whats important, improve on it, add something better. create new styling, effects, motion graphics, etc. lets also restructure the entire flow and ux of the customer portal. I want to create all of this on a separate subdomain somewhere, not connected to anything with sandbox account with balance, be able to buy domains, servers, hosting, etc. but nothing is actually deployed, or provisioned. just so we can test the flow of everything"

They also explicitly said mid-conversation: "i dont want you to lean on the css of the current portal as well, i want you to create a new look to the entire system whilst using similar styling and colors" — meaning: keep the navy/violet/cyan brand hues and the existing icon convention (hand-drawn inline SVG, no library) as continuity anchors, but do NOT reuse the current `.card`/`.btn-*`/component implementations as the base — genuinely new visual system.

They also confirmed, when asked about Phase 2 isolation: fully separate deployment (own app/worker/DB, zero shared state with staging or production), AND clarified further: they want to actually click through paying for things, deploying servers, buying domains — all with fake money, but NOTHING should actually provision/deploy/register for real. Given Stripe itself isn't code-gated anywhere in the real codebase, the safest design for this isolated sandbox is to mock the payment step completely too (not just infra) — no real Stripe calls at all, not even test-mode — so there is zero external dependency of any kind.

One more real constraint to respect: I cannot literally source/scrape real stock photography into a design system delivered as a Claude Artifact — the Artifact CSP blocks all external image loading except Google Fonts. "Beautiful images relevant to context" needs to be delivered as custom SVG illustrations / generative graphics (consistent with how this session has already built things like a hand-rolled 3D canvas globe and custom flag SVGs), not real photos.

## What I need from you

Design a concrete, phased implementation plan:

**Phase 1 (immediate, current scope of work)**: A representative first wave of redesigned page/flow MOCKUPS, delivered as Claude Artifacts (static/lightly-interactive HTML/CSS/JS, private, for the user's approval) — NOT real code changes to the Nxeon repo at all in this phase. Recommend a specific, well-justified set of 3-5 pages/flows to mock up first that would prove out the whole new design language (nav/IA, a conversion-critical wizard flow, a dense utility page, a detail/management page) without attempting all 58 sections at once. For each, specify: what current pain point it addresses, what the new IA/flow looks like, and what makes it "new" visually (not just recolored) while preserving the real brand hues and honest content constraints.

**Phase 2 (only after Phase 1 mockups are approved)**: A fully isolated interactive sandbox environment on its own subdomain, implementing the approved design for real — own systemd services/app process/worker, own Postgres DB (seeded with realistic-looking fake plans/pricing/servers), own nginx vhost (copy the nxeon-staging-admin pattern) + DNS + cert, own .env. Design how "deploy a server"/"buy a domain"/"buy hosting" would work with zero real external calls (no Proxmox, no OVH, no real registrar API, no Cloudflare, no Stripe at all — fully mocked "success" responses) while still feeling like the real flow, and how the fake wallet balance would be seeded/topped up for testing. Recommend whether this should be a genuinely separate codebase fork/subset or the same codebase with a hard "MOCK_MODE" flag added at the actual data-layer (worker job handlers + payment action) — weigh maintainability (staying in sync with real design changes) against true isolation risk.

Give me file-level specificity where the plan touches real code (Phase 2), and a clear reasoning for the Phase 1 page selection. Keep the whole plan focused and concrete — this will be turned directly into a plan document for the user's approval.

- baz: Create professional motion graphics and videos from the terminal. AI-powered composition with multi-track layering, choreography, voiceovers, and Lambda rendering. Gated 5-phase workflow ensures quality.
- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.
- figma:figma-use-figjam: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the FigJam context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.
- figma:figma-use-motion: Motion / animation context for the `use_figma` MCP tool — animating Figma nodes via manual keyframes, animation styles, easing, and timeline duration. Load alongside figma-use whenever a task involves adding, editing, or inspecting animation on a node.
- figma:figma-use-slides: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the Slides context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers a dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:explain-usage: Explain where this session's tokens went, with one simple chart in plain language. Use when the user says things like "explain my usage", "where did my tokens go", or asks for a usage breakdown.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text: # Nxeon Portal Redesign — Phase 1 (Mockups) & Phase 2 (Isolated Sandbox) Implementation Plan Grounded in direct inspection of `/opt/nxeon` (production) and `/opt/nxeon-staging` on this host. Key facts confirmed during this pass (all file paths absolute): - `/opt/nxeon-staging` is a **git clone whose `origin` is the local bare path `/opt/nxeon`** (not GitHub) — staging tracks prod by local git pull, not an independent fork. - `/opt/nxeon-staging/.env` **does** carry live Stripe **test-mode** keys (`sk_test_51Pjihl…`, `pk_test_51Pjihl…`) — confirming the background note that Stripe is not sandbox-gated: even on staging today, checkout actually calls Stripe's test API. This is the exact gap Phase 2 must close by mocking payment entirely. - `/opt/nxeon/scripts/configure-domains.sh` reads `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (`BASE_DOMAIN`, `ADMIN_HOST`, `STAGING_HOST`, `CERTBOT_EMAIL` only) and regenerates exactly `/etc/nginx/sites-available/nxeon` and `/…/nxeon-staging` from those four values — it has no concept of a fourth host. `/etc/nginx/sites-available/nxeon-staging-admin` is a **hand-maintained, non-generated** file that proxies an obscure hostname to the same upstream (`127.0.0.1:3001`) as staging, purely so an admin session and a customer session don't collide in the same browser — this is the literal template to copy for a new hostname pointed at a *new* upstream port. - systemd units (`/etc/systemd/system/nxeon-web.service`, `nxeon-worker.service`, `nxeon-staging-web.service`, `nxeon-staging-worker.service`) are trivial and copyable: `WorkingDirectory`, `EnvironmentFile=/.env`, `ExecStart=npm start` / `npx tsx worker/index.ts`. Staging's `.env` binds `PORT=3000`... actually staging serves off `3001` per the vhost `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:3001` — worth double-checking staging's `PORT=` value at build time — the pattern to replicate is: distinct `WorkingDirectory` + distinct `.env` (with its own `PORT`) + distinct `DATABASE_URL`. - `worker/index.ts` dispatches jobs through one flat `handlers: Record Promise>` map (`PROVISION`, `START/STOP/REBOOT`, `DELETE`, `RESIZE`, snapshot/backup ops, `VOLUME_*`, `GAME_*`, `SYNC_FORWARDS`, `SYNC_FIREWALL`, `SYNC_GAME_DNS`, `CLAUDE_BUILD`…) — `SANDBOX` already short-circuits the real infra calls in ~20 of these branches (confirmed lines: 448, 627, 652–653, 670, 716, 809, 862, 881, 885, 911, 916, 972, 1028, 1034, 1043–1044, 1155, 1235, 1298, 1361, 1445, 1549, 1876, 1934). - `lib/registrar.ts` is a name.com v4 client gated only by `registrarConfigured()` (env presence), not by `SANDBOX` — this is the domain-purchase equivalent of the Stripe gap and needs the same treatment. - `lib/order.ts` (`orderQuote`, `placeOrder`) and `lib/actions.ts` (`payAndDeploy`) contain the real pricing/tax/coupon/wallet-split/promo-eligibility business logic — this is pure DB logic with **no external calls itself**; the external calls are called *from* `payAndDeploy` (Stripe) and from the worker/registrar layer, so this logic is safe and valuable to reuse as-is in the sandbox rather than re-implement. - Confirmed nav (`app/dashboard/layout.tsx:33-96`), confirmed icon convention (`components/portal/Shell.tsx:182-188`, no library, ``. The brand-continuity constraint ("new look, same styling and colors") means every mockup must visibly reuse `--color-brand-500` (#6f47f5), the navy scale (`#060a14`→`#253354`), and `--color-accent-cyan`/`--color-accent-blue`, and must reuse the *convention* of hand-drawn inline stroke-SVG icons (no lucide/heroicons look-alike), while deliberately NOT reusing `.card`/`.btn-*`/`.glass` as literal CSS classes — new surface treatments, new elevation/depth language, new type scale, new motion vocabulary built from scratch. ### Selection rationale: 4 pages/flows, each proving a different dimension of the redesign A full IA overhaul touches ~58 sections; mocking all of them before the user has approved a direction wastes effort if the first draft misses the mark. These four are chosen because together they exercise every distinct *class* of screen in the portal, so approving them de-risks the other ~54: 1. **Dashboard shell + nav (IA backbone)** — `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` (7 flat sections, 20 items) / `components/portal/Shell.tsx` - **Pain point**: sections were merged reactively over time ("Billing + Invoices merged", "Refer & earn + Affiliate merged" — literal comments in the nav array), producing a flat, un-prioritized 20-item list with no sense of "what matters right now" vs. "rarely-touched settings." Compute/Network/Mail/Tools/Account read as arbitrary buckets, not a journey. - **New IA**: Reorganize around customer *intent* rather than product taxonomy — a persistent top-level "Overview" plus 3-4 intent clusters (something like Infrastructure [servers/hosting/games/volumes], Grow [domains/sites/mail/SSL], Build [AI builder/matrix], Account) with a genuinely prioritized order (most-used first, account/settings last), collapsed sub-groups, and a redesigned command palette entry point. Mock the full sidebar + top bar + a populated overview page so the new visual system is visible at every layer. - **What makes it visually new**: replace the flat list-of-links rail with a depth-layered rail (soft floating active-pill with directional glow, not a flat highlight bg), a new custom icon set drawn fresh (not reusing Shell.tsx's existing 20 `icons[]` glyphs, though same 24×24 stroke convention), and an ambient animated background treatment on the overview page (slow-drifting gradient mesh in navy/violet/cyan, CSS-only) replacing the current flat `.card` grid. 2. **VPS Deploy wizard (conversion-critical flow)** — `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx` (1913 lines) + `PaymentStep.tsx` (823 lines) + `WizardReassuranceCard.tsx` - **Pain point**: `DeployWizard.tsx`'s `Stepper` (lines 145-165) is one of 6 divergent step-indicator implementations across the codebase; the wizard is long, dense, and front-loads plan/spec selection before building any purchase momentum. This is also the single highest-leverage page for buyer psychology since it is the primary revenue path. - **New flow**: A single unified stepper component (visual spec only, in this Phase — real component consolidation happens in code later, not in Phase 1) with clearer progressive disclosure: plan tier as a visual comparison (not a dense form), a live-updating price summary that never leaves view (evolve `WizardStickyCart.tsx`'s concept, not its exact styling), and reordering so commitment-building (what you get, real uptime/support/setup facts via `WizardReassuranceCard`) appears earlier, with `PaymentStep.tsx` visually redesigned but conceptually identical (still: card/PayPal/Coinbase, still `PaymentTrustBar`'s "Secured by Stripe" + real card logos, zero invented guarantees). - **What makes it visually new**: plan cards get a "hero tier" treatment with a custom-drawn server/rack SVG illustration per tier (not the current small inline glyph), step transitions get real motion (slide + fade choreography, mocked with CSS transitions/keyframes in the Artifact), and the price panel gets a distinct "receipt" visual metaphor instead of a plain bordered box. 3. **Billing (dense utility page)** — `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx` (944 lines, 10 stacked sections) - **Pain point**: the single worst "organically bolted-on" page in the app — a customer has to scroll past auto-recharge, spend controls, and bandwidth charts just to find their invoices. No hierarchy of "what do I need right now" (e.g., a shortfall warning is buried at a `section-label` at line 288 alongside everything else). - **New flow**: Apply and *extend* the already-proven `?tab=` pattern from `app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx` (lines 26/48-52/94-96) — tabs for Overview (balance + upcoming renewals + any shortfall alert, surfaced prominently), Payment & Auto-recharge, Spend Controls, Transactions & Invoices. This is explicitly "keep what's important [the underlying data/sections], improve the flow" rather than a ground-up rebuild. - **What makes it visually new**: a redesigned balance/spend "cockpit" header (custom SVG gauge/sparkline treatment instead of `components/ui/charts.tsx`'s current bar treatment — new visual language, same dependency-free hand-rolled SVG discipline), tab chrome that's a genuinely new component (not reusing `.nav-item`), status-colored edge treatments for shortfall/paused states that are more prominent than the current `section-label !text-red-300` inline override. 4. **Server detail/management (detail page pattern)** — `app/dashboard/servers/page.tsx` (thin) → `components/customer/ServersList.tsx` (133 lines) → individual server via `ServerTabs.tsx` (111 lines) - **Pain point**: represents the "detail/management" page archetype used across Servers, Hosting, Games, Domains — currently a fairly plain tab bar over stacked cards (console access, metrics, backups, networking, danger zone) with no visual priority given to the things that actually need attention (a failed backup, a suspended state, a resize needed). - **New flow**: A management page with a persistent "status header" (server identity + live state + primary actions: console/restart/resize) always visible above the tabs, an attention-first ordering (alerts/`ProvisionErrorBanner`-equivalent surfaced above routine tabs), and tab content redesigned around task groups (Access, Performance, Data protection, Danger zone) rather than 1:1 with existing component names. - **What makes it visually new**: a custom "server card" identity treatment (a small generative/illustrative rack or node glyph unique per OS/plan family, not the generic rect-based server icon reused everywhere today), redesigned `MetricsPanel`/`DiskUsageChart` visual language building on but not copying `components/ui/charts.tsx`, and a distinct, more serious "danger zone" visual treatment than the current bordered-card approach.
